reassurance_anchor.text_en: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.

verses.translation_en: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What is the context of this verse?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It was revealed in Makkah. The disbelievers had asked for a sign. Allah answered with this verse: peace is in His remembrance.

evidence.arabic: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ
evidence.translation_en: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?'

evidence.arabic: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ
evidence.translation_en: Those who have believed and whose hearts find peace in the remembrance of Allah.
Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.

sub_dropdowns.question: What does 'Dhikr' mean?
sub_dropdowns.answer: In the Quran, it means to hold something in constant awareness, with the heart, the tongue, and action.

evidence.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you.

evidence.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا
evidence.translation_en: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
And the remembrance of Allah is greater.

sub_dropdowns.question: How is Dhikr different from Dua?
sub_dropdowns.answer: Dua is asking, while Dhikr is remembering.

evidence.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
evidence.translation_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.
Call upon Me; I will respond to you.

socratic_dropdowns.question: How does this verse apply in daily life?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It connects remembering Allah with peace of heart.

evidence.arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
evidence.translation_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear.
For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
evidence.translation_en: And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.

verses.arabic_text: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
verses.translation_en: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does 'Wus'aha' mean?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It comes from W-S-A, meaning wide, spacious, encompassing. The verse says the soul's widest capacity.

evidence.translation_en: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth.
evidence.why_cited: The same root describes the vastness of the Throne.

evidence.translation_en: My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.
evidence.why_cited: The same root shows the breadth of knowledge.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does the Quran say about ease?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: Ease is not absent from hardship. The Quran places it alongside hardship and tells us that Allah intends ease for us.

evidence.translation_en: For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

evidence.arabic: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
evidence.translation_en: Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship.
Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.

verses.translation_en: For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Why 'with' and not 'after'?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: The Quran speaks of ease alongside hardship, as something Allah intends, and as something He can make possible.

evidence.translation_en: For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

evidence.arabic: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
evidence.translation_en: Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا
evidence.translation_en: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair.

verses.arabic_text: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
verses.translation_en: And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What does 'Hasbuhu' mean?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: The Quran uses different words to express the same meaning: Allah is sufficient.

evidence.translation_en: Then He is sufficient for him.
Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?
Then indeed, sufficient for you is Allah.

verses.arabic_text: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
verses.translation_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Why is 'say' missing?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: Every other place in the Quran, the command 'say' is used. Here, it is left out. The answer is placed directly after the question.

evidence.translation_en: Say, 'They are measurements of time.'
evidence.why_cited: A nearby verse where 'say' is used.

evidence.translation_en: Indeed I am near.
evidence.why_cited: The “say” is left out. The answer follows directly: “Indeed I am near.”

verses.translation_en: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Who is this verse addressed to?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It is addressed to those who have transgressed against themselves. It is a call to return.

evidence.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ
evidence.translation_en: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves.'
And return to your Lord and submit to Him.

verses.translation_en: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Where was this said?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: In the cave of Thawr, during the Hijrah. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr were together in the cave after being driven out by those who disbelieved.

evidence.arabic: إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا
evidence.translation_en: When he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.'
And Allah sent down His calmness upon him.

evidence.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.translation_en: It is He who sent down calmness into the hearts of the believers.
